clue.text: Previously finished a brief examination

parts.note: once means formerly, at some earlier time
over means ended or done

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having already completed a quick inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick cursory look at something is the idiom for a hasty inspection.

clue.text: Break the law, but not on purpose

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Someone commits a crime but accidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'not on purpose' as one phrase meaning accidentally; the cryptic reading splits it after 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit a crime or transgression, a sense of the verb for wrongdoing.

clue.text: An element found naturally in church capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A chemical element is found naturally occurring in a church in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday name for the metal chromium, a chemical element.

clue.text: Just include price-earnings ratio without concealment

indicators.note: include means the word for just takes the ratio's letters inside it

parts.note: only means merely, just
PE is the standard abbreviation of the price-earnings ratio in finance

explanation.surface: A company is told to disclose its price-earnings ratio transparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicly, frankly, in full view: the adverb for no concealment.

clue.text: Former partner has a job to produce this written commentary

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a position is a post or job

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse's work requires writing an explanatory text.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed explanation or interpretation set out in prose, as a scholarly treatise.

clue.text: Garden produce can be a hazard

indicators.note: read as a verb, produce means make something new out of these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Vegetables from the allotment might prove risky to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a noun (vegetables) but works as a verb, signalling that GARDEN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a source of peril or risk, a straight synonym.

clue.text: These days taping arrangements need modifying

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

indicators.note: arrangements says the letters of the word taping are set out in another order

explanation.surface: Recording procedures nowadays need to be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering or adjusting to suit new conditions: synonyms.

clue.text: Pool resources and attempt to acquire equities

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
equities are shares in a company

explanation.surface: Investors club together and try to buy stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool resources' looks like a finance term matching 'equities', but it defines the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To split costs equally with others is an informal idiom for clubbing together.

clue.text: Dispatch from painter I had accommodated in sympathy

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword standby for an artist

indicators.note: accommodated in means the contraction for I had is housed within the word for sympathy

parts.note: pity is compassion, sympathy
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A message from an artist was received with compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' looks like a message sent, but it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch in the sense of swiftness or promptness, as 'with all dispatch'.

clue.text: Permanently a supporter of strong defences

parts.note: someone for a cause is in favour of it, a supporter
keeps are the fortified central towers of castles

explanation.surface: Someone is a lifelong advocate of building solid fortifications.
explanation.walkthrough: A keep is the stronghold tower at the heart of a medieval castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held to keep forever is held for good, an idiom for always.

clue.text: Refuse to get father's drink

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive S
to sup is to drink, sip

explanation.surface: Someone declines to fetch Dad's beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline or turn down an offer is an idiomatic phrasal verb meaning refuse.

clue.text: Salesmen ordered to be anonymous

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters of the word salesmen are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Sales staff are instructed to keep their identities secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unidentified, with no name given, is anonymous: a synonym.

clue.text: One row of beads found by the sea

explanation.surface: A necklace is discovered washed up on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thread of pearls or beads is one sense; the other is a literary word for shore or beach.

clue.text: Deer country requires no development

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A land full of deer has no need of building projects.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of growth or progress, standstill: a state of no development.

clue.text: A word of thanks to Mr Brown is not to the point

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
tan is a light brown colour
a gent, gentleman, is a man addressed as Mr

explanation.surface: Thanking someone called Mr Brown turns out to be irrelevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Brown' looks like a name, but it is read as a brown (TAN) gentleman (GENT).
explanation.definitionFit: Going off on a digression, wandering from the subject, is the idiom for irrelevant.

clue.text: Eleven considered individually

explanation.surface: A team of eleven players is assessed one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven is written 11: one digit beside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven as numerals is a one set next to a one; the other sense is singly, in turn.

clue.text: Non-crushable suit for an intractable person

explanation.surface: A robust suitcase is recommended for a difficult character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is short for suitcase, a rigid luggage case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid suitcase is one sense; the other is a tough, incorrigible character.

clue.text: Evil leer interpreted as a signal of arousal

indicators.note: interpreted means read in a different way, so the letters of evil leer are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked look is taken as a sign of desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arousal' suggests desire, but means waking: the bugle call that rouses soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call that wakes troops in the morning, a military wake-up signal.

clue.text: More or less ran one huge conglomerate

indicators.note: conglomerate as a verb means gather into a mixed mass, so these letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Someone roughly speaking managed a vast business group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conglomerate' looks like a noun (a big company that 'ran' is running) but it signals mixing RANONEHUGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximately, roughly, close to: the phrase is an idiom for almost.

clue.text: A portion of illicit riches derived from oranges

indicators.note: A portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A share of ill-gotten wealth comes from the orange trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Citric acid occurs in citrus fruit such as lemons and oranges.

clue.text: It tastes hot, but is utterly cold

indicators.note: utterly is read as 'when uttered', so the word for cold is spoken

parts.note: chilly means cold

explanation.surface: Something tastes hot, yet is completely freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like 'completely' but means spoken out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot pepper used to spice food is a fiery-tasting pod.

clue.text: One boy pursuing education became a famous inventor

indicators.note: pursuing means the one boy comes after the word for education

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad pursuing his studies grew up to become a renowned inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva Edison, the American who devised the phonograph and electric lamp.

clue.text: Transatlantic friend needs to obtain financial plan

parts.note: bud is American slang for a pal
get means obtain, acquire

explanation.surface: An American pal needs to secure a spending plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transatlantic' marks BUD as an American word, from the British setter's view.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan of income and spending, as a household or chancellor sets out.

clue.text: Expelled one woman in the orchestra

indicators.note: in places one woman inside the word for the orchestra

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
I is the Roman numeral for one
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A female musician was thrown out of the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven out, exiled, sent away: synonyms for expelled.

clue.text: Appeal to a mass meeting in words

parts.note: O is the exclamation of appeal or invocation, as in 'O Lord'
a rally is a large public gathering

explanation.surface: A speaker addresses a big crowd at a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' looks like a plea to the crowd, but is the single letter O used to call on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, delivered by voice: the adverb for speech.

clue.text: Girl gets around regulation and abuses authority

indicators.note: gets around means the girl's word encloses the word for regulation

parts.note: miss is a young girl or unmarried woman
a rule is a regulation

explanation.surface: A young woman evades a rule and oversteps her powers.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern badly, wielding power unjustly, is to abuse authority.

clue.text: The day before Kelly made the score level

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event, as Christmas Eve
Ned Kelly was the famous Australian outlaw

explanation.surface: On the eve of a match, Kelly drew the teams level.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a nineteenth-century Australian bushranger, the best-known Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Equalised, squared, drew level: synonyms for evening a score.

clue.text: Lack of movement at the front

explanation.surface: Troops at the front lines are idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is one sense as a single word; split into two words it means engaged in combat on the battlefield.
